title: GoFree: Reducing Garbage Collection via Compiler-Inserted Freeing
problem: Garbage collection overhead is a significant performance bottleneck in memory-managed languages like Go; GC pauses and memory reclamation consume substantial CPU and power resources even though not all heap memory requires dynamic collection.
motivation: Reducing GC frequency and cost directly improves application latency, throughput, and energy efficiency by reclaiming reachable-but-unused memory earlier through compiler-directed deallocation.
method: GoFree uses escape analysis—a compiler technique that runs in O(n^2) time to identify short-lived objects that can be safely freed—to insert explicit freeing instructions instead of relying on garbage collection. These freeing operations use thread-safe mechanisms and operate transparently within Go's memory model without changing the garbage collector. The result is fewer garbage collection pauses and lower peak memory usage.
key_novelty: GoFree's core novelty is using O(n^2) escape analysis to automatically insert compiler-based freeing for identified short-lived objects, thereby reducing garbage collection overhead while preserving thread-safety and requiring no modifications to the garbage collector.
contributions: A powerful and efficient escape analysis algorithm (O(n^2)) that identifies short-lived heap objects safe for explicit deallocation
A thread-safe freeing primitive suitable for concurrent environments
Empirical validation showing 7% reduction in GC frequency, 13% reduction in GC time, and 2% wall-clock improvement on real Go programs
limitations: Evaluation limited to 6 open-source Go programs; no analysis of compiler overhead breakdown or sensitivity to object lifetime patterns.
primary_theme: Compiler-directed memory deallocation to reduce GC overhead
